statement: Global data-centre electricity use in 2027 is below the IEA's 2025 base-case projection for 2027 (IEA; 2028 release)
status_at_phase_end: Not resolvable in 2024: the reference projection (IEA 2025 base case) did not yet exist. 2024 context: IEA estimated ~460 TWh data-centre use in 2022, possibly over 1,000 TWh by 2026; a national-lab report gave a wide scenario range for Bloc A data-centre demand to 2028.

items.summary: International energy agency: data centres consumed an estimated 460 TWh in 2022; consumption from data centres, AI and crypto could double, reaching more than 1,000 TWh in 2026.
items.detail: IEA, Electricity 2024 - Analysis and forecast to 2026, executive summary (verified via web_extract this run; release date 2024-01-24 per IEA report listing, not shown in extracted text).

items.summary: A Bloc A national laboratory published a congressionally requested update estimating data-centre electricity use back to 2014 and a scenario range of future demand to 2028.
items.detail: LBNL, '2024 Bloc A Data Center Energy Usage Report', published 2024-12-19, DOI 10.71468/P1WC7Q (verified via web_extract this run; scenario figures not in the extracted abstract, so no value recorded).

items.summary: The benchmark the indicator uses (the agency's 2025 base-case projection for 2027) had not been published by the end of the phase.
items.detail: IEA's dedicated AI/data-centre energy projections appeared in 2025, after the phase window (excluded under the as-of rule). Reference page opened: IEA Electricity 2024.
